# Section X: Kiln Heat-Up and Start-Up (Cold Start)

**Applies to:** 3000 tpd preheater/precalciner kiln line
**Source:** Senior kiln operator shift notes, formalised for the automation control narrative
**Status:** DRAFT. All values marked **[TBC]** need confirmation by process engineering, the refractory supplier, and the ESP/burner OEMs before they are configured in the DCS.

---

## X.1 Purpose and Scope

This section defines the sequence, permissives, interlocks and operator actions for bringing the kiln from cold (ambient) condition to stable feed operation. It covers:

- Main burner light-off on diesel and changeover to coal
- Controlled heat-up to protect the refractory
- Kiln rotation during heat-up (auxiliary and main drive)
- ID fan, gas analysis and ESP protection during firing
- Introduction of raw meal feed and ramp-up
- Kiln protection on loss of power

It does not cover warm or hot restarts after short stops, precalciner burner light-off, or coal mill start-up. These should be written as separate subsections (see X.10).

---

## X.2 Definitions

| Term | Meaning in this section |
|---|---|
| Back-end temperature (BET) | Kiln inlet gas temperature, tag **[TBC]** |
| Inlet analyzer | Gas analyzer at kiln inlet / riser, measuring CO, O₂ (and NOx/CH₄ if fitted), tag **[TBC]** |
| Aux drive | Auxiliary (barring/inching) kiln drive, on emergency power supply |
| Main drive | Main kiln drive motor |
| Shell scanner | Infrared kiln shell temperature scanning system |
| Tower | Preheater cyclone tower |

---

## X.3 Start-Up Permissives (Before Light-Off)

The DCS shall not allow the main burner to be ignited unless all of the following are true:

| # | Permissive | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | ID fan running and at ≥ 60% **[TBC: speed or damper position]** | Operator notes | See X.6.1 |
| P2 | Kiln purge completed: ID fan at purge rate for ≥ **[TBC]** min / **[TBC]** volume changes | Added, standard burner safety practice | Removes combustible gases before ignition |
| P3 | Inlet analyzer healthy, in service, not in calibration or blowback | Added | CO protection depends on it |
| P4 | Aux drive available and on emergency supply; emergency generator available | Operator notes (implied) | See X.8 |
| P5 | Shell scanner healthy and recording | Operator notes (implied) | |
| P6 | Burner primary air fan running | Added | Protects burner tip |
| P7 | Diesel supply pressure/temperature within limits; flame scanner healthy | Added | Burner management system (BMS) |
| P8 | Cooler and kiln hood doors closed; personnel clear of kiln and tower | Added | Safety |
| P9 | ESP HT sets **OFF** | Added, **[TBC]** | See X.6.3 regarding ESP during oil firing |

---

## X.4 Heat-Up Sequence

### Step 1: Light-off on diesel
1. Confirm all permissives in X.3.
2. Ignite the main burner on diesel at minimum firing rate **[TBC: L/h]**.
3. Confirm flame via flame scanner. On flame failure, the BMS trips the fuel, and the kiln must be re-purged before reignition.
4. Keep firing low. The firing rate is governed by the heat-up rate limit in Step 2, not by a fixed setting.

### Step 2: Controlled heat-up (refractory protection)
- **Heat-up rate limit:** 30–50 °C/h at the back end (operator guidance). The refractory supplier's dry-out and heat-up curve takes precedence where it is more restrictive.
- **Automation:** The DCS calculates the rolling BET rate of rise over **[TBC: 15–30]** min.
  - Alarm at rise > 50 °C/h **[TBC]**
  - Firing rate increase inhibited while rise > 50 °C/h
  - Operator alert if rise < 20 °C/h for > **[TBC]** h (stalled heat-up)
- **Hold points:** Add hold points per the refractory supplier curve **[TBC]**. This matters especially after a relining, when a dry-out programme applies.
- **Note:** The operator notes give the rate only at the back end. Confirm with the refractory supplier whether burning-zone or shell temperature limits also apply.

### Step 3: Kiln rotation during heat-up
The kiln must be rotated periodically on the aux drive to prevent thermal bowing of the shell. Rotation frequency increases as temperature rises. Proposed schedule, **all values [TBC]** against the site's current practice:

| BET range | Rotation (aux drive) |
|---|---|
| Ambient – 200 °C | ¼ turn every 60 min |
| 200 – 400 °C | ¼ turn every 30 min |
| 400 – 600 °C | ¼ turn every 15 min |
| 600 – 800 °C | Continuous on aux drive |
| > 800 °C **[TBC]** | Transfer to main drive at minimum speed |

- **Automation:** The DCS issues a rotation prompt or auto-rotation per the schedule above. It alarms if the rotation interval is exceeded by > **[TBC]** min.
- **Transfer to main drive:** Main drive starts at minimum speed **[TBC: rpm]**. Speed increases gradually and is held at low speed until feed is introduced.
- **Interlock:** The aux drive and main drive cannot be engaged simultaneously, per the mechanical interlock / clutch arrangement **[TBC]**.

### Step 4: Changeover from diesel to coal
- **Trigger:** BET ≈ 600 °C **[TBC: confirm setpoint and allowable band, e.g. 580–620 °C]**.
- **Additional permissives (added, [TBC]):**
  - Coal mill / fine coal bin ready, with fine coal bin level > **[TBC]**%
  - Coal dosing system (rotor weigh feeder / screw) ready
  - Fine coal bin CO and temperature normal (coal system fire/explosion protection)
  - Secondary air temperature > **[TBC]** °C for stable coal ignition
- **Sequence:**
  1. Start coal at minimum dosing **[TBC: t/h]** while diesel is still firing.
  2. Increase coal and reduce diesel in steps, holding total heat input approximately constant and respecting the heat-up rate limit.
  3. Shut off diesel once coal flame stability is confirmed (flame scanner, stable BET and O₂) and coal is ≥ **[TBC]** t/h.
- Monitor inlet CO closely during changeover. This is the highest-risk period for incomplete combustion (see X.6.2).

### Step 5: Continue heat-up to feed-ready condition
Continue firing on coal within the heat-up rate limit until the feed permissives in X.5 are met.

---

## X.5 Introduction of Raw Meal Feed

### Feed permissives
| # | Condition | Value |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | BET | 900 – 1000 °C (operator guidance) **[TBC]** |
| F2 | Preheater tower hot: top cyclone outlet temperature | > **[TBC]** °C (operator notes say "tower is hot"; this needs a measurable definition) |
| F3 | Kiln on main drive | At minimum speed **[TBC]** |
| F4 | Inlet O₂ | Within **[TBC]**% |
| F5 | Inlet CO | Below alarm level |
| F6 | Shell scanner | No hot-spot alarms active |
| F7 | Downstream equipment ready | Clinker cooler (grate, fans), clinker transport, raw meal feed system **[TBC]** |

### Feed ramp-up
1. Start feed at approximately 40% of nominal **[TBC: t/h of kiln feed]**.
2. Ramp feed to nominal over a few hours (operator guidance). Proposed: **[TBC]** % increments every **[TBC]** min, or a continuous ramp of **[TBC]** t/h per hour.
3. Increase kiln speed, fuel rate (main burner and calciner, per the calciner light-off procedure) and ID fan proportionally with feed, following the feed/speed/fuel ratio curves **[TBC]**.
4. **Ramp hold conditions:** the DCS holds the feed ramp (does not increase) if any of the following occur:
   - BET falls below **[TBC]** °C
   - Inlet CO in alarm
   - Inlet O₂ below **[TBC]**%
   - Shell scanner hot-spot alarm
   - Cyclone blockage alarm

## X.6 Process Protection During Heat-Up and Start-Up

### X.6.1 ID fan minimum
- **Rule (operator notes):** The ID fan must never go below 60% while the burner is firing.
- **Implementation:**
  - Low clamp of 60% **[TBC: speed or damper]** on the ID fan output whenever the main burner flame is proven
  - Alarm if the ID fan drops below the clamp
  - **Trip:** ID fan stop or speed below **[TBC]**% for > **[TBC]** s trips main burner fuel
- **Clarification needed:** Is "60%" fan speed, damper position, or motor load? This must be defined before configuration.

### X.6.2 CO protection and ESP (explosion risk)
- **Rule (operator notes):** If CO rises at the inlet analyzer, de-energize the ESP. CO in the presence of energized electrodes is an explosion hazard.
- **Implementation (proposed thresholds; all [TBC] against ESP OEM and site safety study):**

| Level | Typical industry range | Action |
|---|---|---|
| CO alarm | ~0.5% vol **[TBC]** | Alarm; operator to correct combustion (increase draft / reduce fuel) |
| CO trip | ~1.0–1.5% vol **[TBC]** | **Automatic trip of all ESP HT sets** |
| ESP re-energize permissive | CO < **[TBC]**% for ≥ **[TBC]** min | Manual reset only, after purge |

- **Analyzer failure:** Loss of the inlet analyzer signal (fault, calibration, blowback) must trip or inhibit ESP HT **[TBC: fail-safe action]**. The ESP must not run blind to CO.
- **Recommendation:** Consider a second CO measurement (e.g. at the ESP inlet) for redundancy, given this is a safety function.
- **Note:** This interlock is a safety function. It should be assessed under the site's functional safety process (e.g. IEC 61511 SIL assessment) rather than implemented only as basic DCS logic.

### X.6.3 ESP during diesel firing
- **Not in operator notes; must be confirmed.** Many plants keep the ESP de-energized during oil firing and early heat-up because of unburnt hydrocarbons and CO risk. Define the condition for first ESP energization **[TBC: e.g. on coal, BET > X °C, CO < Y%]**.

### X.6.4 Shell scanner hot spots
- **Rule (operator notes):** Watch the shell scanner for hot spots.
- **Implementation:**
  - Alarm at shell temperature > **[TBC]** °C (zone-specific limits per refractory zone)
  - High-high alarm at > **[TBC]** °C, with operator action required: reduce firing, adjust flame, or stop the kiln per the refractory damage procedure **[TBC]**
  - Hot-spot alarms inhibit the feed ramp (X.5)
- **Note:** During heat-up, shell temperatures are generally low. A hot spot early in heat-up may indicate missing or damaged refractory and should be treated seriously.

## X.8 Loss of Power During Heat-Up or Operation

- **Rule (operator notes):** On power loss, the kiln must be turned on the aux drive, or the hot shell will bow.
- **Implementation:**
  1. On main power failure, the emergency generator auto-starts and the aux drive supply transfers automatically **[TBC: ATS arrangement and transfer time]**.
  2. The aux drive starts and rotates the kiln, either continuously or at an interval of **[TBC]** min, until the kiln has cooled below **[TBC]** °C.
  3. If the aux drive or generator fails, the DCS raises a critical alarm. The site manual barring/turning procedure applies **[TBC: reference procedure]**.
- **Recommended additional emergency loads (added, [TBC]):**
  - Burner primary air fan, which protects the burner tip from radiant heat
  - Cooler first-compartment fans, which protect the grate
  - DCS / UPS and analyzers
  - Kiln hood and tower lighting
- **Testing:** The emergency generator and aux drive transfer should be tested periodically **[TBC: frequency]**, with results logged.

---

## X.9 Operator Responsibilities vs. Automation

| Function | Automated | Operator |
|---|---|---|
| Light-off permissives and purge | Yes (BMS) | Initiates |
| Heat-up rate limiting | Rate monitoring and inhibit | Adjusts firing within limits |
| Kiln rotation | Scheduled prompts / auto-rotate | Confirms; manual intervention if needed |
| Diesel→coal changeover | Optional sequence **[TBC]** | Initiates and supervises |
| ID fan minimum | Clamp and trip | — |
| CO / ESP protection | Automatic trip | Corrects combustion; resets after clear |
| Feed introduction | Permissive check and ramp | Initiates; may hold ramp |
| Shell scanner | Alarms and ramp inhibit | Assesses and acts |
| Power loss response | Auto generator and aux drive | Supervises; manual turning if needed |

---

## X.10 Open Items for Engineering Review

1. Define ID fan "60%" (speed, damper or load) and the fan trip setpoint.
2. Obtain the refractory supplier heat-up and dry-out curve. Confirm whether the 30–50 °C/h back-end limit is sufficient or whether other temperature limits apply.
3. Confirm the kiln rotation schedule against current practice and the kiln OEM.
4. Confirm the diesel→coal changeover temperature, coal system permissives, and minimum coal rate.
5. Set CO alarm, trip and reset thresholds with the ESP OEM. Carry out a functional safety (SIL) assessment of the CO/ESP trip.
6. Define the ESP energization conditions during heat-up (X.6.3).
7. Define "tower hot" as a measurable temperature condition.
8. Define the feed ramp profile and the feed/speed/fuel/ID fan ratio curves.
9. Set shell scanner alarm limits by refractory zone.
10. Confirm the emergency power arrangement, aux drive transfer, and which loads are on emergency supply.
11. Write companion sections: warm/hot restart, precalciner burner light-off, coal mill start-up, and controlled shutdown/cool-down.
12. Review this draft with the senior operator before he retires. Many of the "[TBC]" values are likely known from his experience and should be captured from him directly.

---

**Notes on this draft:**
- Items explicitly in the operator's notes are marked "operator notes". Items marked "added" are standard industry practice I've included because the notes imply them or a control narrative needs them. They should be validated, not assumed.
- The typical CO ranges quoted are indicative only. Do not configure them without OEM and safety-study confirmation.
- The most valuable next step is probably a short structured interview with the operator using the X.10 list, so his actual numbers replace the [TBC]s.
